The consequence is that there is now more irritation to the gastric mucosa, leading to ulcers. You can ask yourself why they aren't the number one cause of gastric ulcers. The answer is simply that they have been overused. That and the fact that they have a relatively short half life, meaning that they are quickly broken down and removed from the system. What this means is that although stress can cause increased secretion of acid, the cells themselves are not being damaged or destroyed. Articular nerves detect changes in position & pressure/stretch and transmit this information to the spinal cord and brainstem. (There is also some overlap as the dorsal column medial lemniscus carries both proprioceptive and nociceptive information).   Joints have a rich nerve supply provided by articular nerves. Hilton's law states that the nerves supplying a joint also supply the muscles moving the joint and the skin covering their distal attachments. The nerve of a joint transmits impulses which play a key role in proprioception.  proprioception is the ability to sense stimuli arising within the body regarding position, motion, and equilibrium. This sensation is important for motor control and is lost in many neurological disorders. There is a loss of positional inhibition and an inability to distinguish between proprioceptive stimuli and sensory conflict. There is a disturbed body image and a failure to recognize when the limb is malpositioned. Nociception- sensation of pain, temperature, and crude touch. Exteroception- sensation of light touch, crude touch, and vibration. Interoception- sensation of body position, motion, and equilibrium. Kinesthesia- awareness of movement, position, motion, and equilibrium. Answer B is correct. A - incorrect as nociception is the sense of pain, temperature and is responsible for the perception of damaging stimuli. It is mediated by specialized nociceptive nerve endings which have C-fibres. These detect tissue damage and transmit this information to the central nervous system where it causes the experience of pain.  C- Fibres are slow, unmyelinated and polymodal - they are activated by thermal, mechanical & chemical stimuli. They allow for the perception of stimuli following a delay of around 10 - 50 ms. D - Incorrect as this is the sense of internal organs and the body's internal state. This includes the detection of chemical substances, pH, temperature, and metabolic concentrations. E - incorrect as this is the combination of kinesthetic and vestibular sensations. It is the perception of movement and balance. The sense of movement is derived from joint positions and the vestibular system (the inner ear).

The running knee injury here is most likely to be an ACL tear. A common mechanism of the injury here is twisting the knee as you change direction in running and is often accompanied by a 'pop' feeling in the knee. A PCL tear is more commonly caused by either a fall on a hyper flexed knee with the foot plantar flexed or a strike on the front of your tibia with your knee flexed. A patella fracture is commonly caused by following directly on your knee. The first two options are both feasible treatments for an ACL tear. The extent of the damage is often determined by an MRI and usually, most first cases require no surgery. However, this runner has done this injury twice before, suggesting it is recurrent and that her knee may be unstable. Operative therapy would increase the stability of her knee and therefore, this is the best option for her. The third option is also a feasible treatment for an ACL tear but because this is a recurrent injury, she may be less likely to return to full activity without surgery.  The final option is for a stable patella fracture; this means the fracture doesn't break the knee cap. A non-operative approach is used here as it is assumed the fracture won't heal misaligned. This is because a fracture of the patella tends to fragment into the intercondylar notch, holding the extensor mechanism in place. Surgery is only used if there is a significant displacement or if the fracture involves the articular surface. The time frame for recovery is 6 to 8 weeks. Conversely, if there is a rise in citrate (which is up regulated by the process of gluconeogenesis), then the activity of this enzyme will increase. Overall, the activity of this enzyme depends on the concentration of its products and substrates.
